idiom_name: framework-free logic class + injected collaborator interface (GoogleTest and gMock doubles)
implementation_notes: Move the decisions into a plain C++ class that includes no widget or framework headers, and hand the collaborator in through a virtual interface (or std::function for a single operation), so a test constructs the class directly and gMock supplies the double; the slot or callback left behind reads the widgets, calls the class and writes the result back. Where the host is itself a template, the collaborator can instead be a template parameter, which removes the virtual call and the mock but forces the test to instantiate the same template. Keep the runtime interface when the collaborator must vary at run time (tests, platform ports); keep the logic class in its own header and translation unit or the framework's includes and moc output leak into the test target.
pitfalls: gMock verifies expectations when the mock is destroyed, so a double used from a queued or asynchronous callback must live in a fixture whose teardown runs after the event loop has drained; otherwise the test goes green before the slot ever runs.
A logic class declared next to the widget drags framework headers and moc-generated code into the test target; keep the collaborator framework-free or the unit tests stop being unit tests.
The virtual seam costs one indirect call per event; in paint or key paths prefer template injection or a plain function pointer, and mock only interfaces you own (wrap the framework API first).
